names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 15 aprilie, «Sfântul Mucenic Crescent».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Κρήσκης ο Μάρτυρας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 13 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Крискент.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with муч. left off as well, the rank word this source uses for a martyr, which this folder already carries in `types`. The heading leaves no epithet and does not name Myra, which is the first thing the body says. The bare form is shared with `crescens-companion-of-quadratus` and that fold is deliberate and recorded.

Read out of the title on the name link behind this place in the line for 13 апреля ст. ст., name page 1304, «Крискент Мирликийский, мч.», with the rank word left off; the day's own line gives the name in the genitive and the city as a phrase after it. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form. The bare «Крискент» this folder already stores as its Serbian form folds with `crescens-companion-of-quadratus`, which is deliberate and recorded; the Russian form with the city in it joins no fold.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 апреля ст. ст. — «Мч. Крискента, из Мир Ликийских (III).»
source.note: The day's third entry and it carries no typikon icon, so no `rank` is recorded. **It keeps him on the same Julian 13 April as the Ohrid Prologue and not the 15 April of the other two calendars**, and the city in the line — «из Мир Ликийских», out of Myra in Lycia — is this folder's own display name. The name page behind the line (1304) gives «День памяти: 13 апреля» and no other day. **It is also the first source read for this folder to print anything of a date**, «(III)», and that century is now the folder's `dates`; the tension with saint.gr's account is set out in the `dates` note. The day page prints one troparion under «Молитвы», a proper of the two sisters of Bethany, which belongs to the moveable Sunday the page is headed for and names other saints, so no hymn was taken from it; this folder's hymns stand as the Romanian and Greek calendars gave them.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 15 aprilie — «Sfântul Mucenic Crescent»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Κρήσκης ο Μάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him on. The identification is the page's own: «Ο Άγιος Κρήσκης καταγόταν από τα Μύρα της Λυκίας», of Myra in Lycia, a disciple of the Apostle Paul and already old — the same man, on the same day, as doxologia's Sfântul Mucenic Crescent. The page gives him no year: it sets him only «την εποχή της παντοδυναμίας της ειδωλολατρίας», so no `dates` were taken.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.04.2026 (13. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Крискент.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, and **the city in its first line is what identifies him**: „Из града Мира Ликијског“, from the city of Myra in Lycia, which is this folder's own see-city and display name. **The Prologue keeps him on a day neither other calendar does**: doxologia and saint.gr both have him on 15 April and this is the Julian 13 April, two days off and not a style conversion. One row per church, so nothing was moved and nothing displaced. **No date**: the entry gives no year and none was inferred; this folder still has none from any source. New to the folder, out of four sentences: that he was **an honourable and famous citizen** of that city; that he **confessed his faith in Christ publicly and mocked the dead idols**; and that **the pagans put him to death by fire**. The stored form Крискент folds with `crescens-companion-of-quadratus`, which holds the same bare forename and which this folder already relates to; the fold is deliberate and recorded in the run's findings. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Crescent, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

english.text: Thy martyr Crescens, O Lord, in his struggle has won from Thee, our God, the crown of incorruption; for having Thy strength, he overthrew his tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. At his prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Τῷ τῆς πίστεως ζήλω πτερωθεῖς τὴν διάνοιαν, πρὸς ἀθλητικὸς ἀριστείας ἀνδρικῶς προσεχώρησας, καὶ ὤφθης τοῦ Σωτῆρος κοινωνός, βασάνους ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἐνεγκῶν διὰ τοῦτο ἐδοξάσθης παρὰ Θεοῦ, Κρήσκη Θεομακάριστε. Δόξα τῷ δεδωκότι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι διὰ σοῦ, πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης, on the page of Άγιος Κρήσκης ο Μάρτυρας. It is his own and names him.

english.text: Winged in mind by the zeal of the faith, thou didst go forward manfully to the prizes of the contest, and wast shown to be a partaker with the Saviour, having borne torments beyond nature. Therefore thou wast glorified by God, Crescens blessed of God. Glory to him who gave thee strength, glory to him who crowned thee, glory to him who works healings for all through thee.

hymns.text: Ὁ Μάρτυς σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτοῦ, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσατο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· ἔχων γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλεν ἔθραυσε καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτοῦ ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστέ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr — Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, on the page of Άγιος Κρήσκης ο Μάρτυρας. This is the common apolytikion of a single martyr and names nobody; the page prints it under his name, so it is copied whole as the page has it.

english.text: Thy martyr, O Lord, in his contest received the crown of incorruption from thee our God; for having thy strength he cast down the tyrants and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. By his supplications, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Εἰ καὶ ἐν γήρᾳ ἐδέξω τὴν ἄθλησιν, ἀλλά νεάζον ἐκτήσω τὸ φρόνημα, καὶ τὴν ἔπαρσιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καθεῖλες στεῤῥῶς, συνεργόν ἐν ἀγῶσι τὸν Λόγον κτησάμενος· οὗ τὸ πάθος δοξάσας, τῆς τούτου ἐγέρσεως, μέτοχος ὤφθης, ὦ Κρήσκη πολύαθλε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ, on the page of Άγιος Κρήσκης ο Μάρτυρας. It is his own, names him, and turns on his old age, which both calendars make much of.

english.text: Though thou didst receive the contest in old age, yet thou hadst gained a young man's mind, and didst firmly cast down the arrogance of the enemy, having taken the Word as thy fellow-worker in the struggles; and having glorified his passion, thou wast shown a partaker of his rising, O Crescens of many contests.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's line for the Julian 13 April closes «Мч. Крискента, из Мир Ликийских (III).» — the third century, printed as the calendar prints a year. It is the only statement of a date any source read for this folder makes: doxologia.ro's notice gives none, the Ohrid Prologue gives none, and saint.gr sets him only «την εποχή της παντοδυναμίας της ειδωλολατρίας». **One reading pulls earlier and is recorded here rather than averaged in.** saint.gr's page makes him a disciple of the Apostle Paul and already old, which would be the first century; it states no year, so no year of its own stands against this one, and the corpus keeps the Crescens of the Second Letter to Timothy as a separate folder which nothing read here identifies with this man. The century is therefore the Russian calendar's own and the Greek page's reading is left standing beside it, unchosen. `node .tmp/dd.mjs '3rd century'` reads in Russian and Greek. Read 7 October 2026.
